subject: science
stem:
Meena wants to measure the length of her notebook at home, but the end of her plastic ruler is broken and the zero mark is missing. She places one end of the notebook against the 2 cm mark and finds that the other end lines up with the 15 cm mark.
What is the length of the notebook?

options.A: 15 cm, because the far end reads 15 cm
options.B: 13 cm, because 15 cm minus 2 cm is 13 cm
options.C: 17 cm, because 15 cm plus 2 cm is 17 cm
options.D: 2 cm, because the notebook starts at the 2 cm mark

subject: science
stem:
Meena wants to measure the length of her pencil. The zero end of her scale is broken, so she places one end of the pencil at the 2 cm mark. The other end of the pencil is at the 15 cm mark.
What is the length of the pencil?

options.A: 17 cm
options.B: 15 cm
options.C: 13 cm
options.D: 11 cm

subject: science
stem:
Dev's 15 cm scale is broken at the zero end, so he starts at the 1 cm mark and the other end of a pencil is at 8 cm.

What is the pencil's length?

options.A: 8 cm, because that is the number he sees.
options.B: 7 cm: 8 cm minus 1 cm.
options.C: 9 cm, by adding 1 and 8.
options.D: Length cannot be found on a broken scale.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Faiz's 15 cm scale is broken at the zero end. He places one end of a ribbon at the 2.0 cm mark; the other end is at 9.5 cm.

Which claims give the ribbon's length correctly? One or more options may be correct.

options.A: 9.5 cm, because that is the larger mark he reads.
options.B: 7.5 cm: 9.5 cm minus 2.0 cm.
options.C: 11.5 cm: 9.5 cm plus 2.0 cm.
options.D: 7.5 cm by subtracting the starting mark from the ending mark.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Priya wants to measure the length of the curved edge of a round steel plate in her kitchen. She has only a straight metre scale and a piece of thread.
Which method will give the correct length of the curved edge?

options.A: Measure the straight distance between the two ends of the curved edge with the metre scale.
options.B: Lay the thread along the curved edge, then straighten the thread and measure its length with the metre scale.
options.C: Estimate the length by eye, because a curve cannot be measured.
options.D: Measure the diameter of the plate and take that as the length of the curved edge.

subject: science
stem:
Meera wants to measure the length of the curved edge of a round steel plate in her kitchen. She does not have a flexible measuring tape.
Which method gives the most accurate measure of the curved edge?

options.A: Measure the straight distance between the two ends of the curve with a metre scale.
options.B: Lay a thread along the curved edge, straighten the thread, and measure its length with a metre scale.
options.C: Guess the length by comparing the curve with the length of her hand span.
options.D: Measure the diameter of the plate with a ruler and use it as the length of the curve.

subject: science
stem:
Noor has to measure a curved leaf edge.

What should she do?

options.A: Use a straight scale along a chord and call that the edge.
options.B: Lay thread along the curve, then measure the thread on a scale.
options.C: Guess from how green the leaf looks.
options.D: Say curved lengths cannot be measured.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena is describing the position of her school library to her friend Ravi. She says, "The library is 20 m from the main gate."

Which statement about Meena's description is correct?

options.A: The main gate is the reference point because the distance is measured from it.
options.B: The library is the reference point because its position is being described.
options.C: No reference point is needed because the distance is only 20 m.
options.D: Ravi's house is the reference point because he is listening to the description.

subject: science
stem:
Meena is standing in her school playground. Her teacher asks four students to describe the position of a flag post in the ground.

Arun says: "The flag post is 12 m from the classroom wall."
Bhavna says: "The flag post is 9 m from the gate."
Chetan says: "The flag post is 15 m from the water tap."
Divya says: "The flag post is 7 m from the neem tree."

All four students measured correctly. Which statement about the reference points is correct?

options.A: Only one student can be correct, because the flag post can have only one position.
options.B: All four students are correct, because each distance is measured from a different reference point.
options.C: The reference point must always be the gate of the school.
options.D: The flag post itself is the reference point in all four measurements.

subject: science
stem:
Imran says the shop is 200 m from the school gate. The shop sign is brightly coloured.

What makes that a position?

options.A: The 200 m alone, with no fixed point named.
options.B: The school gate as the reference point for the 200 m.
options.C: The colour of the shop sign.
options.D: Any unmarked spot on the ground, with the school gate ignored.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena is sitting inside a moving train. Her brother Rohan is standing on the platform as the train passes by.
Which statement about Meena's state of motion is correct?

options.A: Meena is at rest with respect to the train seat, but in motion with respect to Rohan on the platform.
options.B: Meena is at rest with respect to everything, because she is sitting down and not moving her body.
options.C: Meena is in motion with respect to everything, because the train is moving.
options.D: Meena is in motion with respect to the train seat, but at rest with respect to Rohan on the platform.

subject: science
stem: Meena is sitting inside a bus that is moving along a straight road past a school gate. Which statement about motion and rest is correct?

options.A: Meena is in motion with respect to the book lying on her lap.
options.B: Meena is in motion with respect to the school gate.
options.C: The school gate is at rest with respect to Meena.
options.D: Meena is at rest with respect to everything around her.

subject: science
stem:
A bus looks still to Aditi sitting in it, but moving to Kabir on the road.

Is the bus in motion?

options.A: It cannot be both; motion does not depend on a reference.
options.B: It is at rest relative to Aditi and in motion relative to Kabir.
options.C: It is in motion only when someone names it as moving.
options.D: Rest and motion are the same for every observer.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Priya watches four different moving objects near her home in Jaipur.
Which object is showing linear motion, where the path of the object is a straight line?

options.A: A ceiling fan blade spinning round and round
options.B: A ball rolling straight down a sloping ramp
options.C: The tip of the minute hand of a wall clock
options.D: A swing moving back and forth in a park

subject: science
stem:
Arjun watches different objects moving around him during the day.
Which of these is an example of linear motion?

options.A: The second hand of the wall clock moving around the dial.
options.B: Riya sliding straight down a slide in the park.
options.C: A ceiling fan blade spinning above Meena's head.
options.D: A football curving through the air after Kabir kicks it.

subject: science
stem:
A marble rolls along a metre scale without turning aside. Motions may be called linear, oscillatory, or circular.

How should that motion be classified?

options.A: Oscillatory, because every school motion is to-and-fro.
options.B: Linear, because the path is a straight line.
options.C: Not motion, because the marble is slow.
options.D: Circular, because the marble itself is round.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meera is watching things move on her veranda on a hot afternoon.
She watches the tip of a blade of the ceiling fan and a ball rolling straight across the floor.
Which motion is circular?

options.A: neither the tip of the fan blade nor the rolling ball
options.B: the tip of the fan blade only
options.C: both the tip of the fan blade and the rolling ball
options.D: the rolling ball only

subject: science
stem:
Meera watches the hands of the wall clock in her classroom and also sees her brother Arjun riding the giant wheel at the village fair.
Which of these motions is an example of circular motion?

options.A: A ball rolling straight down the corridor of Meera's house
options.B: The tip of the minute hand of the wall clock as it moves
options.C: Arjun cycling in a straight line along the road to school
options.D: A swing moving to and fro after one push

subject: science
stem:
Esha whirls an eraser on a thread so the eraser moves on a circular path. She also rolls a marble along a winding, curving track that is not a circle, and pushes a toy car straight across the floor.

Which motion is circular?

options.A: The marble on the winding track, because its path is not a straight line.
options.B: The eraser on the thread, because its path is circular.
options.C: The toy car on the floor, because it keeps moving while she pushes.
options.D: Both the eraser and the marble, because neither path is a straight line.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
In her house in Jaipur, Meena watches four different moving things during the day.
Which one shows oscillatory motion, that is, motion to and fro about a fixed position?

options.A: A ceiling fan blade going round and round
options.B: The pendulum of an old wall clock swinging about its rest position
options.C: A ball rolling down the playground slide
options.D: A cycle moving straight along the road to school

subject: science
stem:
Meera watches different objects in motion around her home and school. She wants to identify which one shows oscillatory motion — motion that moves to and fro about a fixed position.
Which of the following is an example of oscillatory motion?

options.A: The minute hand of the wall clock moving around the dial
options.B: The swing in the park moving back and forth after Rohan pushes it
options.C: A ball rolling in a straight line across the classroom floor
options.D: A bus travelling from Chennai to Madurai along a highway

subject: science
stem:
A swing moves to and fro about its rest position.

How should that motion be classified?

options.A: Linear, because it is in a playground.
options.B: Oscillatory: to-and-fro about a fixed position.
options.C: Not motion unless it goes in a circle.
options.D: Linear, because the seat is a straight plank.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena lists the materials used to make some objects in her home. Which statement about objects and their materials is not correct?

options.A: A steel tiffin box is made from only one material, metal.
options.B: The same material, wood, can be used to make both a chair and a table.
options.C: The material of an object is always whatever the object is called.
options.D: A school bag can be made from a combination of materials such as cloth and plastic.

subject: science
stem: Meera observes a steel spoon in her kitchen at home. Which statement about the spoon is not correct?

options.A: The spoon is made from one material, steel.
options.B: Steel is the material used to make the spoon.
options.C: The material of the spoon is 'spoon', because the object is called a spoon.
options.D: The same material, steel, can also be used to make a plate or a glass.

subject: science
stem:
Chetan looks at a glass tumbler filled with water.

Which list names the materials the tumbler is made from?

options.A: Glass.
options.B: Glass and water.
options.C: Tumbler.
options.D: Water.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Amit looks at a steel spoon resting in a ceramic bowl of water.

Which list names the materials the spoon is made from?

options.A: Steel.
options.B: Steel and water.
options.C: Spoon.
options.D: Water and ceramic.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena's teacher asks the class to group objects by a common property. Which statement about grouping objects is not correct?

options.A: A steel spoon, a steel plate and an iron nail can be grouped together because they are all made of metal.
options.B: Grouping objects always means putting any objects together, even when no common property is used.
options.C: A red ball, a red pencil and a red eraser can be grouped together because they share the same colour.
options.D: A cotton shirt, a woollen cap and a silk scarf can be grouped together because they are all made of fabric.

subject: science
stem:
Priya is sorting objects in her kitchen cupboard for a school science project. She makes four groups:

Group 1 – a steel tumbler and an iron tava
Group 2 – a plastic spoon and a plastic bowl
Group 3 – a cotton towel and a woollen shawl
Group 4 – a glass tumbler and a steel spoon

In which group has she classified the objects using the common property 'the material they are made from'?

options.A: Group 1 only
options.B: Groups 1 and 2
options.C: Groups 2 and 3
options.D: Group 4 only

subject: science
stem:
Yusuf groups a metal spoon, a steel plate, and a copper coin as metals. He also talks about grouping by colour.

What common property is he using for the metals group?

options.A: Each metals group must hold only one object.
options.B: They share material properties of metals.
options.C: Any two metals alone would still make the group, even if the third object were left out.
options.D: Grouping by colour is the only correct grouping for these objects.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Vikram puts a steel spoon, a copper coin, and an aluminium plate in one group. He says they belong together as metals.

What common property is he using for this classification?

options.A: They share material properties of metals.
options.B: Each metals group may hold only one object.
options.C: Grouping by shiny colour is the only correct grouping for these objects.
options.D: The metals group is correct only when exactly three objects are always present.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena and Arjun are choosing materials for objects needed at home.

1. A stainless steel tumbler is chosen for drinking water because it does not rust and is easy to clean.
2. A rough rubber sole is chosen for chappals because it grips the wet bathroom floor.
3. A thin plastic sheet is chosen as a raincoat for the monsoon because it is soft and colourful, even though it tears easily and leaks at the seams.
4. A glass window pane is chosen for the classroom because sunlight must pass through it.

Which two choices correctly match the material's properties to the object's purpose?

options.A: 1 and 2
options.B: 1 and 3
options.C: 2 and 4
options.D: 3 and 4

subject: science
stem:
Meena wants to stitch a bag to carry her schoolbooks in the rainy season.

The cloth she chooses should be ……1…… so that the books stay dry, and ……2…… so that the bag does not tear under the weight of the books.

Which words correctly complete gaps 1 and 2?

options.A: 1 waterproof; 2 strong
options.B: 1 absorbent; 2 strong
options.C: 1 waterproof; 2 soft
options.D: 1 absorbent; 2 soft

subject: science
stem:
Lata needs a handle that will not get too hot on a pan.

What should she check in the material?

options.A: Whether the material looks shiny.
options.B: Whether its properties fit the use, such as conducting heat poorly.
options.C: Whether it is a metal, because every metal handle stays cool.
options.D: Whether material properties matter for objects — they do not.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Anika needs a pan handle that will not get too hot.

What should she check in the material?

options.A: Whether the material looks shiny.
options.B: Whether its properties fit the use, such as conducting heat poorly.
options.C: Whether it is a metal, because every metal handle stays cool.
options.D: Whether material properties matter for objects — they do not.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena sees a shiny object in her classroom and wants to decide if it is a metal. Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Materials with typically shiny surfaces are said to be lustrous.
options.B: Any object that looks shiny must be a metal, even if it is only painted or coated.
options.C: Metals usually have a lustrous appearance.
options.D: A polished wooden surface can shine without being a metal.

subject: science
stem: Priya sees a steel spoon, a freshly polished wooden bowl, a copper tumbler, and a clay pot on her grandmother's kitchen shelf in Madurai. The polished wooden bowl shines brightly. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The wooden bowl must be a metal because it shines brightly.
options.B: The bowl looks lustrous because of polishing, but its shine alone is not proof that it is a metal.
options.C: The bowl is non-lustrous, so it cannot be a metal.
options.D: Only clay pots can be polished to look shiny, so the bowl is a metal.

subject: science
stem:
Ira holds a new steel plate up to the light. She asks whether shine, weight, the brand name, or letting light through is the right test for a lustrous material.

How should she judge if the material is lustrous?

options.A: By whether it looks shiny, allowing that dirt can hide the shine.
options.B: By whether the plate feels heavy in her hand.
options.C: By the printed brand name on the plate.
options.D: By whether light passes through the plate.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Preeti holds a shiny steel spoon and a shiny plastic bangle up to the light.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: Both look lustrous; shine alone does not prove that a material is a metal.
options.B: Only the spoon can look shiny, because only metals are lustrous.
options.C: The bangle must be a metal because it shines.
options.D: A material is lustrous only if light passes through it.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena tests four materials by pressing them with her thumb and by trying to scratch each one with her fingernail.

1. a rubber eraser that dents easily when pressed
2. a steel spoon that does not dent or scratch easily
3. a cotton pillow that changes shape easily when pressed
4. a glass plate that resists scratching

She calls a material soft if it changes shape or is scratched easily, and hard if it does not.

Which two materials should Meena call soft?

options.A: 1 and 2
options.B: 1 and 3
options.C: 2 and 4
options.D: 3 and 4

subject: science
stem:
Meena presses four materials with her thumb to test whether they are hard or soft. A material is hard if it is difficult to compress or change its shape, and soft if it changes shape easily under pressure.

Which material should Meena classify as hard?

options.A: a lump of wet clay that flattens when she presses it
options.B: a steel spoon that keeps its shape when she presses it
options.C: a rubber eraser that dents when she presses it
options.D: a cotton ball that squashes when she presses it

subject: science
stem:
Harish presses and gently scratches four classroom materials. Soft materials change shape or scratch easily; hard materials resist both.

Which judgement is correct?

options.A: The steel desk edge that neither dents nor scratches easily is hard.
options.B: The stone tile is soft; it dented when he pressed with all his strength.
options.C: The soft rubber eraser is hard, and the steel edge is soft.
options.D: He cannot judge the wooden ruler; a scratch test cannot show hardness.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Yuvraj presses and gently scratches a rubber eraser and a steel spoon edge. Soft materials change shape or scratch easily; hard materials resist both.

Which judgement is correct?

options.A: The eraser that dents and scratches easily is soft; the steel edge that resists both is hard.
options.B: The eraser is hard because it changed shape when pressed.
options.C: He can call the steel edge soft without pressing or scratching it.
options.D: Soft and hard apply only to the steel edge, not to the rubber eraser.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Priya holds different materials up to the light during a class activity in her school in Jaipur.

A clear glass tumbler that lets objects be seen clearly through it is ……1…… .

A frosted glass window pane that lets objects be seen, but not clearly, is ……2…… .

Which words correctly complete gaps 1 and 2?

options.A: 1 transparent; 2 opaque
options.B: 1 transparent; 2 translucent
options.C: 1 translucent; 2 transparent
options.D: 1 opaque; 2 translucent

subject: science
stem:
Meera tests four materials in her home by holding each one in front of a page of her notebook. The table shows what she sees through each material.

Which materials are transparent?

options.A: W and X
options.B: W and Y
options.C: X and Y
options.D: Y and Z

rows: the words on the page are seen clearly
the page is seen but the words look blurred
the words on the page are seen clearly
nothing on the page can be seen

subject: science
stem:
Farid looks through three sheets: clear cellophane, frosted glass, and cardboard.

Through clear cellophane he sees objects clearly. Through frosted glass he sees objects, but not clearly. Through cardboard he cannot see objects at all.

Which classification is correct?

options.A: Clear cellophane is translucent; frosted glass is transparent; cardboard is opaque.
options.B: Clear cellophane is opaque; frosted glass is translucent; cardboard is transparent.
options.C: Clear cellophane is transparent; frosted glass is translucent; cardboard is opaque.
options.D: Clear cellophane is transparent; frosted glass is opaque; cardboard is translucent.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Rhea holds three sheets up to the window: clear plastic, tracing paper, and thick cardboard. Through clear plastic she sees objects clearly. Through tracing paper she sees objects, but not clearly. Through cardboard she cannot see objects at all.

parts.text: How should she classify the clear plastic?

options.text: transparent
translucent
opaque

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meera's teacher asks her to test some materials from her kitchen by stirring each one into a glass of water. Which material will dissolve completely in water and is therefore soluble?

options.A: Sand collected from the garden
options.B: Salt from the kitchen jar
options.C: Fine chalk powder from school
options.D: Ground mustard seeds from the masala dabba

subject: science
stem: Meena adds a spoonful of a material to a glass of water and stirs it well. The material disappears completely and the water looks clear. Which material did Meena most likely add?

options.A: sand
options.B: chalk powder
options.C: salt
options.D: mustard oil

subject: science
stem:
Pooja stirs sugar, sand, and cooking oil into separate glasses of water and waits. Some mixtures look cloudy.

Which statement correctly classifies solubility for solids and other materials?

options.A: Sugar that disappears completely is soluble; sand that remains undissolved is insoluble.
options.B: Sugar that disappears completely is insoluble; sand that remains undissolved is soluble.
options.C: Cooking oil cannot be called soluble or insoluble, because solubility applies only to solids.
options.D: Sand that remains undissolved is still soluble if the water looks cloudy.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Ravi wants to compare two objects at home to find which has more mass. He knows that the heavier object has more mass and the lighter object has less mass.

Which of Ravi's conclusions about mass is correct?

options.A: A small steel spoon has more mass than a large plastic bucket because steel is a metal.
options.B: A full water bottle feels heavier than an empty one, so the full bottle has more mass.
options.C: Two identical steel glasses have different masses because they are kept in different rooms.
options.D: A big ball of cotton has more mass than a small iron nail because the cotton ball is bigger.

subject: science
stem:
Meena fills two identical steel bowls, each half full. One bowl has uncooked rice and the other has cotton wool. The bowl with rice feels much heavier than the bowl with cotton wool.

What can Meena correctly conclude?

options.A: Both bowls have the same mass because they are identical bowls filled to the same level.
options.B: The bowl of rice has more mass because rice is the heavier material.
options.C: The bowl of cotton wool has more mass because cotton wool is fluffier and takes up more space.
options.D: The masses cannot be compared because rice and cotton wool are different materials.

subject: science
stem:
Varun compares a small steel spoon and a large foam packing block. On a balance, the spoon is heavier than the foam block.

What can he correctly conclude about mass?

options.A: The spoon has more mass than the foam block.
options.B: The spoon has more volume than the foam block because it is heavier.
options.C: The spoon has less mass than the foam block even though it is heavier on the balance.
options.D: He cannot compare their masses on the balance.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena fills two identical steel tumblers with different amounts of water. Which statement about the volume of water is not correct?

options.A: The tumbler with the higher water level has the greater volume of water.
options.B: Two identical tumblers can hold different volumes of water if filled to different levels.
options.C: Because the tumblers have the same capacity, they must contain equal volumes of water.
options.D: The volume of water in a tumbler can be judged from the space the water occupies.

subject: science
stem:
Meena pours all the water from a tall, narrow bottle into a short, wide jug. The jug is only half full, while the bottle was completely full.

What should Meena conclude about the volume of the water?

options.A: The volume of water decreased because the jug is only half full.
options.B: The volume of water stayed the same because the same water now occupies a different-shaped space.
options.C: The volume of water increased because the jug is wider than the bottle.
options.D: The volume of water became equal to the full capacity of the jug.

subject: science
stem:
Sneha pours water into two glass tumblers that are the same shape and size. Tumbler P has water up to a higher mark than tumbler Q. Volume means the space the water occupies, not only each tumbler's full capacity.

Which conclusion about volume is correct?

options.A: Tumbler P contains a larger volume of water because the water occupies more space.
options.B: Both tumblers contain equal volumes of water because they have the same capacity.
options.C: Tumbler P and tumbler Q must hold equal volumes whenever their shapes match.
options.D: Tumbler Q holds more water than P because more empty space remains above its lower water mark.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meera lists four things she notices at home during the evening.

1. The wooden stool in the kitchen
2. The beam of light from her father's torch
3. The air inside a football
4. The shadow of the peepal tree outside

Which two things are matter?

options.A: 1 and 2
options.B: 1 and 3
options.C: 2 and 4
options.D: 3 and 4

subject: science
stem: Meena's teacher writes four things on the board: sunlight, air in a football, the smell of agarbatti, and a steel spoon. Meena says, “Air is not matter because we cannot see it.” Which statement about matter is correct?

options.A: Air is not matter because it cannot be seen.
options.B: Anything that occupies space and has mass is matter, so the air in the football is matter.
options.C: Only hard solids like the steel spoon are matter.
options.D: The smell of agarbatti is matter because it spreads in the room.

subject: science
stem:
Amit's class decides what counts as matter. Matter must occupy space and have mass.

Which choice is correct?

options.A: Air in a sealed balloon is matter: it takes up space and has mass.
options.B: Something is matter if it is hard and has volume, even with no mass.
options.C: A beam of torch light is matter: it fills the space it travels through.
options.D: Air is not matter: we usually cannot see it.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena dips her left hand in cold water and her right hand in warm water for a minute. She then puts both hands into the same bowl of water at room temperature. The water feels warm to her left hand but cool to her right hand.
What should Meena do to decide how hot or cold the water in the bowl really is?

options.A: Trust her left hand, because it feels the water as warm
options.B: Measure the water with a thermometer, because touch can give different results for the same water
options.C: Trust her right hand, because it feels the water as cool
options.D: Decide the water has no fixed temperature, since both hands feel it differently

subject: science
stem:
Meena dips one hand in a bowl of warm water and her other hand in a bowl of cool water for a minute. She then puts both hands together into a third bowl of water at room temperature.
To one hand the water feels warm and to the other it feels cool, but a thermometer in the third bowl shows one steady reading.
What does this activity show?

options.A: The water in the third bowl is both warm and cool at the same time.
options.B: Our sense of touch cannot always judge hotness or coldness reliably, so temperature must be measured with a thermometer.
options.C: The thermometer reading changes depending on which hand touches the bowl.
options.D: Warm water and cool water mix to make the thermometer stop working.

subject: science
stem:
Nisha puts one hand in warm water and the other in cool water. Then she puts both hands into the same basin of tap water.

Can she trust touch to say whether the tap water is hot or cold?

options.A: Yes. Touch still tells the true temperature of the tap water.
options.B: No. The two hands disagree, so she should measure.
options.C: Yes. The hand that was in warm water feels the true temperature.
options.D: No. The tap water has two temperatures at once.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Rohan holds one hand under a warm tap and the other under a cool tap. Then he puts both hands into the same bucket of room water.

parts.text: Can he trust touch alone to say whether the room water is hot or cold?

options.text: No. The two hands disagree, so he should measure the temperature.
Yes. Touch still tells the true temperature of the room water.
Yes. The hand that was under the warm tap feels the true temperature.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:

Sneha compares how fast equal amounts of water dry. She uses a shallow wide plate and a narrow-necked bottle. She can also change temperature and how humid the air is. She asks whether water must boil before it can evaporate.

Which prediction is correct?

options.A: With the same amount, temperature, and humidity, water in the shallow wide plate evaporates faster than in the narrow-necked bottle.
options.B: The wide plate always finishes first, even if it holds much more water.
options.C: With temperature and exposed area equal, water evaporates faster in humid air than in dry air.
options.D: Water near room temperature cannot evaporate at all until it boils.

author: grok

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
On a hot afternoon in Jaipur, Meena wipes her forehead and notices that she feels cooler when the fan is on and her skin is damp with sweat.

Her Science teacher explains: The sweat on Meena's skin ……1…… by taking heat from her body.

Because of this, her skin feels ……2…… .

Which words correctly complete gaps 1 and 2?

options.A: 1 evaporates; 2 cooler
options.B: 1 evaporates; 2 warmer
options.C: 1 condenses; 2 cooler
options.D: 1 condenses; 2 warmer

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem: Meena wets the clay roof of her house with water on a hot afternoon in Jaipur. After some time, the roof feels cooler. Why does this happen?

options.A: The water evaporates and takes heat away from the roof
options.B: The water stops the Sun's rays from reaching the roof
options.C: The clay roof releases cold air when it gets wet
options.D: The water becomes ice on the hot roof

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
Varun feels cooler after sweating during a games period, and his grandmother sprinkles water on the terrace roof on a hot day.

Why can evaporation make skin or a roof feel cooler?

options.A: As liquid water evaporates, it takes heat from the skin or roof, so those surfaces feel cooler.
options.B: Water vapour condenses into sweat on the skin, and that condensation cools the skin.
options.C: Water at the same temperature as the roof cools the roof just by wetting it, even if none evaporates.
options.D: Sweat evaporates because the skin has already become cooler.

author: grok

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem: On a monsoon morning, Meera's teacher asks why the water vapour rising from the warm fields near her village in Kerala later returns as rain. Which sequence correctly shows how water vapour becomes clouds and then rain, hail, or snow?

options.A: Water vapour rises, cools, condenses into tiny droplets forming clouds, and the droplets grow and fall as rain, hail, or snow
options.B: Water vapour rises and collects overhead as invisible vapour, which falls directly as rain without forming droplets
options.C: Water vapour cools because it first condenses into cloud droplets near the ground, and these then rise to form clouds
options.D: Cloud droplets turn dark and immediately fall as rain the moment each tiny droplet forms

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
Meena sees tiny droplets on the outside of a steel glass of cold water on a humid afternoon in Chennai. Her teacher explains that water vapour in the air touches the cold glass and changes into liquid droplets.

What is this process called?

options.A: Evaporation
options.B: Melting
options.C: Condensation
options.D: Freezing

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
Harsh watches white clouds form after a cool morning, and later sees rain falling. The chapter also mentions hail and snow.

Which statement best describes how water vapour becomes clouds and then rain?

options.A: Water vapour cools high in the air, condenses into tiny liquid droplets that form clouds, and those droplets may later join and fall as rain, hail, or snow.
options.B: Clouds are thick patches of water vapour that have not yet turned into liquid droplets.
options.C: As soon as tiny cloud droplets form, every cloud must start raining at once.
options.D: A cloud begins to rain only because it looks dark from the ground.

author: grok

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
Meera learns that in the water cycle, water evaporates from oceans and Earth's surface into the atmosphere and later returns to Earth as rain, hail, or snow.

Which process does not return water from the atmosphere back to Earth's surface?

options.A: rain falling on Meera's school playground
options.B: water evaporating from a lake near her village
options.C: hail falling during a winter storm
options.D: snow falling on the mountains

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
Meera notices that wet clothes hung on the terrace of her home in Jaipur dry faster on a sunny afternoon.

In the water cycle, what is happening to the water in the clothes?

options.A: It condenses and falls back as rain.
options.B: It evaporates and enters the atmosphere as water vapour.
options.C: It flows down through the soil to become groundwater.
options.D: It freezes and stays stored as ice on the clothes.

subject: science
chapter_label: A journey through states of water
stem:
Leena draws the path of water for a class poster: wet clothes drying on a terrace, clouds over a river, and rain filling a school tank.

Which statement correctly describes the water cycle?

options.A: Water evaporates into the air, may form clouds, returns as rain or snow, and can move as rivers or groundwater before evaporating again.
options.B: Clouds form when water vapour falls straight back as rain without first becoming tiny droplets.
options.C: Rivers mainly carry ocean water inland so land always gets fresh water from the sea.
options.D: Groundwater under the soil is not part of the water cycle.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena's grandmother is working in the kitchen. In which task is she separating a mixture mainly to remove a component that is not wanted?

options.A: Picking out small stones from a bowl of rice before cooking.
options.B: Collecting tea leaves on a strainer so the flavoured tea can be drunk.
options.C: Churning curd to collect butter for making ghee.
options.D: Evaporating seawater in shallow ponds to collect salt.

subject: science
stem:
Meena's mother is cooking dal for dinner. Before cooking, she washes the dal and pours away the cloudy water containing dust and small stones. Later, she churns curd to collect the butter from it.

Which statement correctly describes the purpose of each separation?

options.A: Washing the dal collects the useful dust, and churning removes the unwanted butter.
options.B: Washing the dal removes an unwanted component, and churning collects a useful component.
options.C: Washing the dal collects a useful component, and churning removes an unwanted component.
options.D: Both washing the dal and churning the curd are done to remove unwanted components.

subject: science
stem:
Komal picks small stones out of uncooked rice, and she collects cream while churning milk for butter.

What is true about these separations?

options.A: Picking stones removes an unwanted part; churning collects a useful part.
options.B: Both actions only remove unwanted parts.
options.C: Both actions are only stirring food, so they are not separations.
options.D: Picking stones collects a useful part; churning removes an unwanted part.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Rohan picks grit out of uncooked dal. Kavita collects butter while churning curd.

What is true about these separations?

options.A: Picking grit removes an unwanted part; churning collects a useful part.
options.B: Both actions only remove unwanted parts.
options.C: Both actions are only stirring food, so they are not separations.
options.D: Picking grit collects a useful part; churning removes an unwanted part.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena is helping her grandmother in the kitchen. They have four different mixtures at home.

1. a few small stones mixed with rice grains
2. salt dissolved in water
3. iron filings mixed with sand
4. oil mixed with water

For which mixture is handpicking the most suitable method of separation?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 3 only
options.D: 4 only

subject: science
stem:
Meena is helping her grandmother in the kitchen. They have a bowl of wheat grains mixed with some small stones and a few pieces of husk. Her grandmother wants to remove the unwanted pieces before grinding the wheat.

In which situation is handpicking the most suitable method of separation?

options.A: When the mixture contains a very large quantity of tiny sand particles spread evenly through the wheat.
options.B: When the unwanted pieces are few in number and large enough to be seen clearly and picked out by hand.
options.C: When the unwanted material is dissolved in water along with the useful material.
options.D: When one solid in the mixture is attracted by a magnet and the other is not.

subject: science
stem:
Diya has a small handful of wheat with a few husk pieces. The husk pieces differ in colour and size from the wheat, and she can pick them out by hand.

Is handpicking suitable for this sample?

options.A: Yes. The components differ and can be picked out by hand.
options.B: No. Handpicking is unsuitable whenever husk is present.
options.C: Yes. Handpicking works for any amount of wheat and husk.
options.D: No. Handpicking cannot separate pieces that differ in colour.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Tara has a small handful of wheat mixed with a few husk pieces. The husk pieces differ in size and colour from the wheat, and she can pick them out by hand.

When is handpicking suitable for this mixture?

options.A: When the components differ and can be separated by hand in a small sample.
options.B: Whenever any solid mixture contains wheat, in any amount.
options.C: Only when the unwanted pieces are identical to the wheat in size and colour.
options.D: Never, because handpicking cannot separate pieces that differ in colour.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena's grandmother brings home bundles of freshly harvested wheat stalks. The grains are separated from the stalks when the stalks are ……1…… . The light husk mixed with the loose grains is then removed by ……2…… .

Which words correctly complete gaps 1 and 2?

options.A: 1 winnowing; 2 threshing
options.B: 1 threshing; 2 winnowing
options.C: 1 threshing; 2 sieving
options.D: 1 winnowing; 2 sieving

subject: science
stem:
Meena's grandmother brings freshly harvested wheat stalks from their field in a village in Punjab. The grains are still attached to the stalks and must be separated before the husk can be removed.

Which statements are correct?

1  Threshing is needed first because the grains are still attached to the stalks, and beating the stalks detaches the grains.
2  After threshing, winnowing can be used to separate the lighter husk from the heavier grains by allowing wind to blow through the mixture.
3  If the grains were already loose and free from the stalks, threshing would not be needed before winnowing.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 2 and 3 only

statements.text: Threshing is needed first because the grains are still attached to the stalks, and beating the stalks detaches the grains.
After threshing, winnowing can be used to separate the lighter husk from the heavier grains by allowing wind to blow through the mixture.
If the grains were already loose and free from the stalks, threshing would not be needed before winnowing.

subject: science
stem:
Nikhil's uncle brings harvested wheat stalks. The grains are still stuck to the stalks.

What should they do first before they try to separate grains from husk?

options.A: Thresh the stalks to detach the grains, then separate husk from the loose grains.
options.B: Call the beating of the stalks winnowing, because air will also blow during the work.
options.C: Skip threshing, because grains still on stalks can go straight into husk separation.
options.D: Blow hard over the unthreshed stalks so the grains fall off by themselves.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Dhruv's uncle brings harvested wheat stalks. The grains are still stuck to the stalks.

What should they do first before they try to separate grains from husk?

options.A: Thresh the stalks to detach the grains, then separate husk from the loose grains.
options.B: Call the beating of the stalks winnowing, because air will also blow during the work.
options.C: Skip threshing, because grains still on stalks can go straight into husk separation.
options.D: Blow hard over the unthreshed stalks so the grains fall off by themselves.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena's grandmother has mixed some paddy grains with their light husks and wants to separate them by winnowing. In which situation will winnowing successfully separate the two parts of the mixture?

options.A: In a closed room where there is no moving air at all
options.B: On a windy day in an open courtyard, where the moving air carries the light husks farther away
options.C: On a still day, by simply leaving the mixture in a heap on the ground
options.D: In a closed container that is shaken gently without any air movement

subject: science
stem:
Meena is helping her grandmother clean rice on their farm in Punjab. Three statements about winnowing are listed. Which statements are correct?

1  Winnowing separates heavier and lighter parts of a mixture using moving air.
2  When the mixture is dropped from a height in a breeze, the lighter husk is carried farther away than the heavier rice grains.
3  Winnowing can also be used to separate the removed skins from peanuts when there is moving air.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 2 and 3 only

statements.text: Winnowing separates heavier and lighter parts of a mixture using moving air.
When the mixture is dropped from a height in a breeze, the lighter husk is carried farther away than the heavier rice grains.
Winnowing can also be used to separate the removed skins from peanuts when there is moving air.

subject: science
stem:
Leena helps clean freshly threshed rice outdoors on a breezy afternoon. She wants to separate light husk from heavier rice grains.

When can winnowing work?

options.A: When moving air carries the lighter husk farther while heavier grains fall closer.
options.B: When the air is still, if she shakes the mixture hard enough.
options.C: When the heavier rice grains travel farther in the wind than the light husk.
options.D: When the two parts look different in colour, even if they have the same weight.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Alok helps clean freshly threshed wheat outdoors. He wants to separate light husk from heavier wheat grains.

When can winnowing work?

options.A: When moving air carries the lighter husk farther while heavier grains fall closer.
options.B: When the air is still, if he shakes the mixture hard enough.
options.C: When the heavier wheat grains travel farther in the wind than the light husk.
options.D: When the two parts only look different in colour but have the same weight.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meera wants to separate mixtures at home using a sieve. Sieving works when the particles of one part are small enough to pass through the holes while the bigger particles stay on the sieve.

For which mixture will sieving NOT work?

options.A: separating bran from wheat flour
options.B: separating small stones from rice
options.C: separating salt dissolved in water
options.D: separating tea leaves from sand

subject: science
stem:
Meena wants to separate a mixture of fine sand and small pebbles using a sieve in her kitchen.

For sieving to work, the holes in the sieve must let the smaller particles pass through while the bigger particles stay on the sieve.

Which row correctly describes when sieving is suitable?

options.A: particles have different sizes: sieving works; particles have the same size: sieving does not work
options.B: particles have different sizes: sieving does not work; particles have the same size: sieving works
options.C: particles have different sizes: sieving works; particles have the same size: sieving works
options.D: particles have different sizes: sieving does not work; particles have the same size: sieving does not work

subject: science
stem:
Harsh needs to separate fine atta from larger bran pieces using a kitchen sieve.

Which choice is correct?

options.A: Use holes between the sizes of the bran and the fine atta so bran stays on top and atta passes through.
options.B: Use holes larger than both the bran and the atta; both will still separate cleanly.
options.C: With holes between their sizes, the fine atta stays on the sieve and the bigger bran falls through.
options.D: Sieving will also remove dissolved sugar from sweetened water poured through the same sieve.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Ovi needs to separate fine rice flour from larger husk pieces using a kitchen sieve.

Which choice is correct?

options.A: Use holes between the sizes of the husk and the fine flour so husk stays on top and flour passes through.
options.B: Use holes larger than both the husk and the flour; both will still separate cleanly.
options.C: With holes between their sizes, the fine flour stays on the sieve and the bigger husk falls through.
options.D: Sieving will also remove dissolved salt from salty water poured through the same sieve.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meera's mother dissolves salt in water while cooking at home. Meera wants to get the salt back from the salt solution. Which method will recover the salt from the solution?

options.A: Filtering the solution through filter paper
options.B: Heating the solution so the water evaporates, leaving the salt behind
options.C: Adding more salt to the solution
options.D: Cooling the solution in a refrigerator

subject: science
stem: Meena's mother dissolved salt in water while cooking, and the solution was accidentally spilled into a clean steel bowl. Meena wants to recover the salt as a dry solid. Which method should she use?

options.A: Evaporate the water by gently warming the solution until the water has gone
options.B: Filter the solution through filter paper to catch the salt
options.C: Cool the solution in a refrigerator so the salt freezes out
options.D: Use a magnet to pull the salt out of the water

subject: science
stem:
Komal's mother dissolves rock salt in water, then wants the dry salt back from the leftover solution. She asks about warming, sunlight, bubbles, and collecting a jug of pure liquid water.

What should she do?

options.A: Allow the water to evaporate completely so the dissolved salt is left as a solid.
options.B: Warm the solution only briefly; dry salt appears as soon as the liquid feels warm.
options.C: Evaporate the water and also collect a jug of pure liquid water from that same simple step alone.
options.D: Wait for sunlight to make the solution bubble; without bubbles the salt cannot return.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Faiz dissolves rock salt in water. He wants the dry salt back from the leftover solution.

Which claims correctly say how evaporation can recover the dissolved solid? One or more options may be correct.

options.A: Allow the water to evaporate completely so the dissolved salt is left as a solid.
options.B: Warm the solution only briefly; dry salt appears as soon as the liquid feels warm.
options.C: Let the water leave as vapour until only the solid salt remains.
options.D: Wait for sunlight to make the solution bubble; without bubbles the salt cannot return.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena lists four mixtures from her home and school laboratory.

1. muddy pond water with sand settled at the bottom
2. salt dissolved completely in water
3. water with fine tea leaves resting at the bottom of the pan
4. sugar dissolved completely in milk

She lets each mixture stand undisturbed and then gently pours off the liquid.

For which mixtures can this method separate the liquid from the heavier matter?

options.A: 1 and 3
options.B: 1 and 2
options.C: 2 and 4
options.D: 3 and 4

subject: science
stem: Meena's mother mixes different things with water at home. She leaves each mixture undisturbed for some time and then gently pours off the water. Which mixture can be separated from the water by this method?

options.A: salt stirred into water
options.B: sugar dissolved in water
options.C: sand mixed into water
options.D: lemon juice squeezed into water

subject: science
stem:
Nikhil leaves muddy water from washing vegetables undisturbed in a tall glass. After the mud settles, he carefully pours off the clearer water.

Which statement is correct?

options.A: Sedimentation lets heavier mud settle, and decantation pours off the liquid above it.
options.B: The settling of mud at the bottom is itself called decantation.
options.C: The same settling-and-pour method will separate dissolved salt from salt water.
options.D: After pouring, no tiny mud particle can remain in the liquid that was poured off.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Priya mixes some fine chalk powder into water in her science class and wants clear water. Decantation alone works only when the solid particles ……1…… at the bottom of the vessel.

Filtration is then needed, because the filter paper holds back particles that are ……2…… than its pores.

Which words correctly complete gaps 1 and 2?

options.A: 1 settle quickly; 2 smaller
options.B: 1 do not settle easily; 2 larger
options.C: 1 settle quickly; 2 larger
options.D: 1 do not settle easily; 2 smaller

subject: science
stem:
Meena's mother asks her to clean the muddy water collected in a pot after washing the courtyard. Meena wonders whether simply pouring off the water (decantation) is enough, or whether she must filter it.

Which statements about separating solid particles from a liquid are correct?

1  Decantation alone removes very fine mud particles that remain floating in water.
2  Filtration is needed when the solid particles are too fine to settle down on their own.
3  Filtering tea through a strainer separates the tea leaves from the liquid.
4  Filtration can separate dissolved salt from salt water.

options.A: 1 and 2
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4
options.D: 1 and 4

statements.text: Decantation alone removes very fine mud particles that remain floating in water.
Filtration is needed when the solid particles are too fine to settle down on their own.
Filtering tea through a strainer separates the tea leaves from the liquid.
Filtration can separate dissolved salt from salt water.

subject: science
stem:
Leena has cloudy water with very fine mud after cleaning a courtyard pot. Pouring off the top liquid still leaves the water cloudy.

What should she conclude?

options.A: Filtration through a fine cloth or filter is needed because many particles are too small to settle and pour off cleanly.
options.B: A coarse cloth alone will catch every mud particle smaller than its holes.
options.C: She should switch to a filter with larger pores than the mud particles so the water clears faster.
options.D: Pouring off the top liquid is enough for every cloudy mixture, including this fine mud.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena's mother wants to make butter at home. She has fresh curd ready in a large bowl. In which situation is churning the suitable method to obtain butter or cream?

options.A: When salt has to be recovered from salty water
options.B: When butter has to be separated from curd made from milk
options.C: When sand has to be removed from drinking water
options.D: When small stones have to be picked out of rice

subject: science
stem:
Meena's grandmother makes butter at home in their village kitchen. She adds a little water to fresh dahi (curd) and churns it with a wooden madhani until white lumps of butter collect on top.

Which statements about this method of separation are correct?

1  Churning is a suitable method for obtaining butter from curd.
2  Churning works because agitating the curd makes the lighter fat separate from the liquid.
3  Churning can also be used to separate salt dissolved in water.
4  The liquid left behind after the butter separates is buttermilk.

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1 and 4 only
options.C: 1, 2 and 4
options.D: 2, 3 and 4

statements.text: Churning is a suitable method for obtaining butter from curd.
Churning works because agitating the curd makes the lighter fat separate from the liquid.
Churning can also be used to separate salt dissolved in water.
The liquid left behind after the butter separates is buttermilk.

subject: science
stem:
Gita churns a bowl of curd. Fatty lumps collect, and a liquid remains. She is deciding which part is butter and which part is buttermilk.

Which statement is correct?

options.A: The fatty lumps are butter, and the remaining liquid is buttermilk.
options.B: The fatty lumps are buttermilk, and the remaining liquid is butter.
options.C: Both the fatty lumps and the remaining liquid are butter.
options.D: Churning leaves the curd unseparated, so neither butter nor buttermilk forms.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Meena wants to clean up mixtures quickly at home and in the school lab. She knows that handpicking takes a long time when the pieces are very small.

In which situation can Meena use magnetic separation instead of handpicking?

options.A: separating small iron nails mixed with sawdust from a carpenter's workshop
options.B: separating large stones mixed with rice in a kitchen
options.C: separating sand mixed with salt on a plate
options.D: separating marigold petals mixed with rice grains for a puja

subject: science
stem:
Meena is helping her grandmother clean rice for cooking. She notices small iron nails mixed with the rice grains in the container.

She wants to remove the nails quickly without touching each one by hand.

Which method should Meena use, and why?

options.A: Handpicking, because iron nails are too small to be attracted by a magnet.
options.B: Magnetic separation, because iron is magnetic and the magnet can pull the nails out of the rice.
options.C: Magnetic separation, because a magnet can pick any visible solid out of a mixture.
options.D: Handpicking, because a magnet will attract the rice grains along with the nails.

subject: science
stem:
Harsh finds small iron nails mixed with sawdust and wants a quick clean-up without picking each nail by hand.

Which method is suitable?

options.A: Use a magnet to pull out the iron nails.
options.B: Use a magnet to pull out aluminium scraps mixed the same way.
options.C: Use a magnet on a pile of only iron nails and scrap iron to sort them from each other.
options.D: Avoid the magnet for tiny iron bits; magnetic separation needs pieces large enough to pick by hand.

author: grok

subject: science
stem: Meena is helping her grandmother clean up the kitchen after some things got mixed together. Each method of separation uses only one difference in properties. Which mixture needs a sequence of more than one separation method to separate it completely?

options.A: Iron nails mixed with sawdust, which can be separated with a magnet.
options.B: Sand, common salt and water mixed together, which must be separated step by step.
options.C: Pebbles mixed with water, which can be separated by filtering.
options.D: Salt dissolved in water, which can be separated by evaporation.

subject: science
stem: Meena's mother gives her a mixture containing sand, common salt and water. Meena wants to collect each part separately. Which statement is correct?

options.A: One single method is enough because every mixture can be separated completely if the method is done carefully.
options.B: She needs more than one method in a sequence: filter to get the sand, then evaporate the water to get the salt.
options.C: Filtering the mixture once will collect the sand, the salt and the water separately at the same time.
options.D: Evaporating the water first will give pure salt, leaving no need for any other step.

subject: science
stem:
Komal has a mixture of sand, common salt, and water. She must collect each part separately by filtration and evaporation of the filtrate.

Which plan is correct?

options.A: Filter to separate the sand, then evaporate the filtrate to recover the salt; water is removed in that evaporation step.
options.B: Sand and water alone always need several different separation methods in a long chain.
options.C: One careful filtration separates sand, salt, and water all at once into three pure parts.
options.D: Evaporate all the water first, then filter the dry sand-and-salt powder to obtain pure salt.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Multiple choice question: Meena finds four things in her school garden in Jaipur. She wants to know which one is living. She should check whether it shows all the life characteristics such as needing food, growing, respiring, responding to stimuli, and reproducing. Which of the following statements is correct ( )
A. A plastic ball lying in the garden is living because it can roll when pushed.
B. A neem sapling is living because it needs water and air, grows, respires, and can reproduce.
C. A dry, fallen leaf on the ground is living because it was once part of a tree.
D. A moving toy car is living because it shows movement like an animal.

options.A: A plastic ball lying in the garden is living because it can roll when pushed
options.B: A neem sapling is living because it needs water and air, grows, respires, and can reproduce
options.C: A dry, fallen leaf on the ground is living because it was once part of a tree
options.D: A moving toy car is living because it shows movement like an animal

subject: science
stem:
Multiple choice question: Meena's grandmother says that a dry rajma seed kept in a jar for many months is still a living thing. Which of the following reasons best supports grandmother's statement ( )
A. The seed shows all life processes like active growth and movement while lying in the jar
B. The seed is living because it has the ability to germinate and show life processes when given water, air and warmth
C. The seed is non-living because it does not move from place to place like an animal
D. The seed is living because it is hard and brown in colour

options.A: The seed shows all life processes like active growth and movement while lying in the jar
options.B: The seed is living because it has the ability to germinate and show life processes when given water, air and warmth
options.C: The seed is non-living because it does not move from place to place like an animal
options.D: The seed is living because it is hard and brown in colour

subject: science
stem:
Anjali finds a dry dormant mustard seed, a rooted flowering hibiscus, and a toy car near her school garden. She wants to decide which is living.

Which choice uses the shared life characteristics correctly?

options.A: The dry dormant mustard seed is dead because it is not moving or growing right now.
options.B: The rooted flowering hibiscus is living because it shows life processes such as growth, needing food, and responding to surroundings.
options.C: The rooted flowering hibiscus is non-living because plants cannot move from place to place.
options.D: The toy car rolling down a slope is living because it shows movement.

author: grok

subject: science
stem:
Leela finds a dry dormant mustard seed, a potted mint plant, and a toy bus near the garden. She wants to decide which is living.

Which claims use the shared life characteristics correctly? One or more options may be correct.

options.A: The dry dormant mustard seed is dead because it is not moving right now.
options.B: The potted mint plant is living because it shows life processes such as growth and needing food.
options.C: Living things are judged by shared life characteristics, not by one visible feature alone.

options.B: The forest has many tall trees, so it must be a home for many life forms.
options.C: The forest looks green from far away, so many life forms can live there.
options.D: The forest is a home only for large wild animals that need space to move.

subject: science
stem: During a nature walk near her school in Pune, Meera sees a small park with only a few rows of teak saplings and, nearby, a large wooded area thick with many kinds of trees, shrubs and grasses, where birds, squirrels and insects live. Her teacher asks why the wooded area is called a forest that supports many life forms. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The wooded area is a forest because its green colour attracts many animals to live there.
options.B: The wooded area is a forest because its dense and varied plant growth provides food and shelter for many animals, birds and insects.
options.C: The wooded area is a forest because many animals live there, and that is why dense and varied plants grow in it.
options.D: The wooded area is a forest because it is a home for large wild animals, though birds and insects cannot live in it.

stem:
Ajay's science walk near a reserve forest shows dense herbs, shrubs and trees with birds, insects and deer.

options.C: Dense, varied plant growth provides food and shelter, so many animals, birds and insects can live there together.
options.D: Any patch of green plants is the same kind of forest home because it is green.

stem:

subject: science
stem: Meena's teacher asks her to collect a spoonful of soil from the school garden in Jaipur. After looking at it closely, Meena writes down what the soil is most likely to contain. Which of her statements is correct?

options.C: Soil contains only water that collects when rain falls on the ground.

stem:

What is this soil most likely to contain, and how was it formed?

options.A: Only sand; it formed in a few days when rainwater first touched the rocks
options.B: Sand, worms, tiny organisms, and decayed plants; it formed over thousands of years as rocks were broken down by the Sun, water, and living things
options.C: Only worms and insects; it formed in one rainy season from decayed leaves
options.D: Only large pieces of rock; it forms immediately when a rock cracks in the Sun

subject: science
stem:
Chetan digs a small pit in the garden and examines the soil with a hand lens. He thinks about sand, insects, worms, tiny organisms, decayed plant and animal matter, and rocks broken by rainwater over time.

Which statement about soil is correct?

options.A: Soil and sand are the same material.
options.B: Soil forms immediately the first time rainwater cracks a rock.
options.C: Soil can contain sand, insects, worms, tiny organisms, and decayed plant and animal matter, and it forms over a long time as rocks break apart.
options.D: Soil never contains organisms too small to see with the naked eye.

Which statement about rocks, minerals, and metals is correct?

options.A: Rocks, minerals, and metals are different names for the same thing, so they can be used without any limit.
options.B: Minerals are made up of rocks, and metals are made up of minerals.
options.C: Rocks are made up of minerals, from which metals are extracted, and they must be used responsibly because they form very slowly.
options.D: Only rocks used in buildings need to be conserved; minerals used to make metal products do not.

stem:

options.A: Rocks are made up of metals, and rocks can be used without limits because they are visible everywhere.
options.B: Minerals are made up of rocks, and only rocks used for buildings need to be conserved.
options.C: Rocks are made up of minerals, metals such as iron and copper are extracted from minerals, and rocks form so slowly that they must be used responsibly.
options.D: Rocks, minerals, and metals are different names for the same thing, so there is no need to conserve them.

subject: science
stem:

Which statement is correct?

options.A: Rocks are made up of metals such as iron and copper.
options.B: Minerals are made up of rocks.
options.C: Rocks are made of minerals; metals such as aluminium, copper and iron are extracted from minerals; rocks and minerals form slowly, so they should be used carefully.

options.D: Wood and dung cakes are fossil fuels because they are burned for cooking.
